checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is the gas limit minimum of 5000 (GAS_LIMIT_MINIMUM) enforced by check_gas_limit before block acceptance?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Identify the check_gas_limit function in the Osaka fork specification (osaka/fork.py, SG-015). 2. Verify that the function checks gas_limit < GAS_LIMIT_MINIMUM (5000) and returns False when violated. 3. Trace all callers of check_gas_limit to confirm it is invoked during block header validation for blocks received over P2P. 4. Construct a test block with gas_limit = 4999 (just below minimum) and verify the block is rejected. 5. Construct a test block with gas_limit = 5000 (exactly minimum) and verify it is accepted. 6. Verify that an attacker-controlled proposer cannot gradually lower gas_limit toward the minimum across consecutive blocks, each staying within the adjustment factor (parent_gas_limit // 1024).
executable_checks: Unit test: submit block header with gas_limit = 4999, assert block is rejected
Unit test: submit block header with gas_limit = 5000, assert block is accepted
Unit test: verify gas_limit = 0 is rejected
Property-based test: forall blocks accepted by check_gas_limit, gas_limit >= 5000
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0051, Trust Boundary: tb-012, Source Invariant: SG-015/INV-002, Threat: stride-017. A proposer sets gas limit below 5000. If accepted, blocks cannot include even minimal transactions.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does process_system_transaction always set origin and caller to SYSTEM_ADDRESS (0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe)?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the process_system_transaction function in osaka/fork.py (SG-008). 2. Verify that TransactionEnvironment is constructed with origin=SYSTEM_ADDRESS. 3. Verify that the Message is constructed with caller=SYSTEM_ADDRESS. 4. Check all code paths to ensure no alternative path can set origin or caller to a different address. 5. Trace all callers of process_system_transaction (process_checked_system_transaction, process_unchecked_system_transaction) to confirm they do not override the origin/caller. 6. Verify that system contracts (beacon deposit, withdrawal request, consolidation request, block hash) called via this function receive msg.caller == SYSTEM_ADDRESS. 7. Attempt to construct a scenario where a non-SYSTEM_ADDRESS caller interacts with system contracts as if privileged.
executable_checks: Unit test: call process_system_transaction and assert tx_env.origin == SYSTEM_ADDRESS
Unit test: call process_system_transaction and assert message.caller == SYSTEM_ADDRESS
Integration test: execute a system contract call and verify msg.sender inside the EVM is SYSTEM_ADDRESS
Negative test: attempt to call system contract from a non-SYSTEM_ADDRESS and verify it is not treated as a system transaction
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0052, Trust Boundary: tb-004, Source Invariant: SG-008/INV-001. If the system address is set incorrectly, system contracts receive calls from unexpected callers, potentially bypassing caller-based access controls. Bug bounty eligible: must demonstrate a system transaction executing with a caller other than SYSTEM_ADDRESS.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Is system transaction gas fixed at exactly SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_GAS (30,000,000)?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the process_system_transaction function in osaka/fork.py (SG-008). 2. Verify that TransactionEnvironment is constructed with gas_price=0 and gas=SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_GAS. 3. Confirm that SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_GAS is defined as Uint(30_000_000) and is not overridable by parameters. 4. Check all callers of process_system_transaction to ensure none pass a different gas value. 5. Verify that process_checked_system_transaction and process_unchecked_system_transaction do not modify the gas parameter before or after calling process_system_transaction. 6. Review whether any fork-specific changes could alter this constant.
executable_checks: Unit test: call process_system_transaction and assert tx_env.gas == 30_000_000
Unit test: verify SYSTEM_TRANSACTION_GAS constant equals Uint(30_000_000)
Integration test: execute system contract and verify gas limit in EVM context is 30,000,000
Negative test: attempt to trigger system transaction with different gas allocation and verify it is rejected or not possible
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0053, Trust Boundary: tb-004, Source Invariant: SG-008/INV-002, Threat: stride-008. Incorrect gas allocation could cause system contract failures (too low) or resource waste (too high). Bug bounty eligible: must demonstrate system transaction executing with gas != 30,000,000.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Do system transactions strictly enforce should_transfer_value=False and value=0 to prevent ETH creation or destruction?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the process_system_transaction function in osaka/fork.py (SG-008). 2. Verify that the Message object is constructed with should_transfer_value=False. 3. Verify that the Message object is constructed with value=Uint(0) or equivalent zero value. 4. Trace the should_transfer_value flag through the EVM execution to confirm that no ETH transfer occurs during process_message_call when this flag is False. 5. Check that the SYSTEM_ADDRESS balance is not affected after system transaction execution. 6. Verify that the target system contract's balance is not affected by the system transaction call. 7. Construct a proof-of-concept where should_transfer_value=True is set for a system transaction and demonstrate ETH creation or destruction. 8. Review all system contract call sites (beacon deposit, withdrawal request, consolidation request, block hash) to ensure none bypass this constraint.
executable_checks: Unit test: call process_system_transaction and assert message.should_transfer_value == False
Unit test: call process_system_transaction and assert message.value == 0
Integration test: execute system transaction and verify no balance change on SYSTEM_ADDRESS or target contract
Property-based test: forall system transactions, pre_balance(SYSTEM_ADDRESS) == post_balance(SYSTEM_ADDRESS)
Negative test: demonstrate that setting should_transfer_value=True would cause ETH supply violation
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0054, Trust Boundary: tb-004, Source Invariant: SG-008/INV-003, Threat: stride-008. CRITICAL: Value transfer in system transactions could create or destroy ETH, affecting total supply integrity. Bug bounty eligible: must demonstrate a system transaction transferring non-zero value.

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does make_receipt correctly set succeeded = (error is None) to ensure receipt correctness for consensus?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the make_receipt function in osaka/fork.py (SG-007). 2. Verify that the Receipt is constructed with succeeded=(error is None). 3. Test with error=None: verify succeeded=True. 4. Test with error set to a valid EVM error: verify succeeded=False. 5. Check edge cases: empty error string, zero-length error, None vs. empty distinction. 6. Verify that the succeeded field propagates correctly into receipt encoding via encode_receipt. 7. Verify that receipt_root computation uses the succeeded field, so any mismatch would cause consensus divergence. 8. Trace how the error value flows from process_message_call output into make_receipt to ensure no intermediate transformation corrupts the error-to-succeeded mapping.
executable_checks: Unit test: make_receipt(error=None) returns receipt with succeeded=True
Unit test: make_receipt(error=SomeError) returns receipt with succeeded=False
Property-based test: forall (error, receipt) pairs from make_receipt, receipt.succeeded == (error is None)
Consensus test: verify receipt_root matches expected value for blocks with mixed success/failure transactions
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0055, Trust Boundary: tb-006, Source Invariant: SG-007/INV-001, Threat: stride-018. Incorrect receipt succeeded field causes receipt_root divergence, leading to consensus failure. Bug bounty eligible: must demonstrate a receipt where succeeded != (error is None).

checklist.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity: Does make_receipt compute bloom filter correctly via logs_bloom(logs) for consensus-critical receipt encoding?
checklist.test_procedure: 1. Locate the make_receipt function in osaka/fork.py (SG-007). 2. Verify that the Receipt is constructed with bloom=logs_bloom(logs). 3. Trace the logs_bloom function implementation to verify it processes all log addresses and topics through keccak256 hashing and 3-iteration bit manipulation. 4. Test with empty logs: verify bloom is all zeros (empty bloom). 5. Test with a single log containing one topic: verify bloom matches expected value. 6. Test with multiple logs containing multiple topics: verify bloom is the OR of all individual bloom contributions. 7. Verify that the computed bloom propagates into receipt encoding and ultimately into receipt_root. 8. Verify that block-level bloom (logs_bloom aggregated across all receipts) matches the header bloom field. 9. Test edge cases: logs with empty topics, logs with maximum number of topics, very long log data.
executable_checks: Unit test: make_receipt with known logs produces expected bloom filter
Unit test: logs_bloom([]) returns zero bloom
Unit test: bloom filter for single log with address and topic matches EIP-specification
Property-based test: forall logs, make_receipt(logs).bloom == logs_bloom(logs)
Cross-client test: compare bloom output with reference implementation for same log set
checklist.notes: Source: PROP-0056, Trust Boundary: tb-006, Source Invariant: SG-007/INV-002. Incorrect bloom filter computation causes receipt_root mismatch and block bloom mismatch, both consensus-critical checks. Bug bounty eligible: must demonstrate bloom filter mismatch causing consensus divergence.
